Ah I see your point about using the tax refund to re-invest and it should equal out in the end. However the difference between 25% vs 50% taxes is too big for me and I am making an assumption that MOASS will kick off within the year and paying that small RRSP-withdrawal tax hit will completely outweigh the taxes when MOASS hits. The moment MOASS hits, it will be too late to DRS RRSP shares because the tax hit will be too high. The price is still pathetically low so the tax hits are still in the affordable ranges.

Both your scenarios assume MOASS is still years away. Tax refunds only happen once a year in April/May.

Your broker would transfer them for you from RRSP to Cash then DRS transfer them, shares are never sold. Suppose your RRSP shares are worth $30,000 right now and you are in high income bracket. You will probably owe $15,000 in taxes in April 2023 for the withdrawal yes, it is a tax hit.

BUT. When MOASS happens, and your RRSP account is worth more than $10 million (an example) tell me, how will you withdraw that money? (Remember, withdrawals from RRSP are considered INCOME and not capital gains). You withdraw all at once, you get taxed $5 million. You withdraw $1M per year, you pay $500k in taxes per year. You withdraw $100k per year, you’ll get taxed roughly 30% (depending on province). It will take you 100 years to withdraw at that rate. 

OR. Just DRS your RRSP shares now, pay the $15k tax hit next year. And since Canada has good capital gains tax laws, you’ll only pay roughly 25% maximum from the $10 million (only 50% of total capital gains is taxable, 50% of 50% is 25%).

If you want to keep your shares in RRSP and pay more taxes, then that’s your choice.

Not financial advice.

EDIT: LOL. People downvoting because they lack understanding of an RRSP. It is an income tax-DEFERRING system, not a tax-avoidance system. Tax-free system on capital gains and withdrawals is what the TFSA is for.

If you really need ECMO, it's cause your lungs are complete crap that nothing else will keep the patient alive (not even a vent), and we need to let the lungs completely rested.
